notes_list.title: Carbocation Rearrangement Check
notes_list.basic_overview: Friedel–Crafts alkylation can involve carbocation-like electrophiles, so hydride or alkyl shifts may change the final carbon skeleton.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
When predicting a product, draw the most stable carbocation or carbocation-like intermediate before aromatic attack. Friedel–Crafts acylation avoids this particular rearrangement issue because the acylium ion is resonance stabilized.

MECHANISM & STEPWISE EXPLANATION
The source describes the transformation as: Friedel–Crafts alkylation can involve carbocation-like electrophiles, so hydride or alkyl shifts may change the final carbon skeleton. The mechanism should be read as activation of the stated substrate, formation of the key reactive intermediate, the bond-making/bond-breaking event described by the reaction, and the stated work-up/product-forming step.

1. Activate the stated substrate with the listed reagent/conditions.
2. Generate the key reactive intermediate or electrophile/nucleophile implied by the reaction.
3. Carry out the characteristic bond-forming, bond-breaking or rearrangement step.
4. Complete proton transfer/work-up and verify the characteristic product.
